To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

domain specific model integration can be achieved by combining model transformation languages, that model transformation languages can be combined to achieve model integration, and that this is possible by using an object-oriented mechanism.

domain-specific model integration languages can (i) be defined by specifying declarative transformation rules, (ii) be composed to achieve complex model transformations and model integration tasks, (iii) rely on object-oriented techniques to implement the transformations.

domain-specific integration languages can be used for model management, that they can be composed to achieve more complex model management tasks, and that the implementation of such integration languages can be based on a categorization of model transformations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to implement model management tasks in a domain specific way.
the definition of a domain specific model integration language that is used to specify the global model management task.
the development of model transformation systems that allow the specification of complex model management tasks in a declarative and modular way, which can be executed efficiently.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented approach provides a powerful and flexible framework for model management.
the proposed approach is a very powerful tool for developing complex model management systems.
the proposed approach allows for the definition of model integration languages that can be composed in a flexible way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

model integration languages can serve as the glue for the integration of different transformation approaches, thus allowing for the implementation of complex model management tasks in a declarative manner.
we show how model management can be implemented in a scalable way by using model integration languages.

we are able to define domain specific model integration language and to compose them in order to achieve a complex model management task, such as model merging, model migration or model synchronization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
